bot_chento_v3_eth.method: Per pool row sorted by t: E = t+15m, X = exit_bar_ts+15m, stop_pct = risk/entry. Cooldown: skip if E - E_last_taken < 6h (exact 6h passes) -> 0 skips, 184 taken. No 48h skip on ETH (FILTER_NO_TILT is BTC-only, strategy/config.py:83). Half-after-loss (TILT_HALF_AFTER_LOSS=True, chento_v3_eth/config.py:31; runner.py:132-136): scale=0.5 if the taken trade with the latest X among taken trades with X < E lost on GROSS price, sign*(exit_price-entry) < 0 with no cost (runner.py:80-90), else 1 -> 106 halved, 0 ambiguous exit-time ties. Scale is applied to RISK_PCT before the cap (runner.py:97-99). Sizing: notional_x = min(0.02*scale/stop_pct, 3) with CAPITAL_USDT=10,000, RISK_PCT=2.0, NOTIONAL_MAX_X=3.0 (chento_v3_eth/config.py:15,17,18; botlib.py:527-528); 1 trade at cap; fixed capital (runner.py:138). Per-trade % of capital = 100 * notional_x * stop_pct * R = 100*pnl_usdt/10,000 at 10 bp RT on notional charged at close (trades.py:341-342,356), cross-checked from prices: max abs diff 2.6e-14 %. No funding (apply_funding=False, signal.py:504-508). Stop at stop price, 6R target, 72h TIF, ladder off, OKX gate off - baked into CSV R. Values rounded to 4 dp; sum 129.956% = review's ETH ungated production additive total +129.957% (recon_summary KEY ETH_ungated_prod_total_return_pct_additive); count 184 matches; per-exit-year sums match the review's per-year table (2025: -8.84%).
bot_chento_v3_eth.caveats: 1) Pool fidelity 334/337 = 0.991, precision 1.0 (results/fidelity_ETH.json); pool cooldown runs on anchors, live on executed entries (README.md:445-450) - no ETH skip rule removes triggers, so this matters less than on BTC. 2) In-sample: dials selected on overlapping history; only 2 of 184 taken trades (sum -2.18%) have t after the 2026-07-20 P1 cutoff; mean likely optimistic, so AMBER fires more than nominally. 3) Non-stationary: mean by exit year 2021 -0.54, 2022 +1.09, 2023 +2.31, 2024 +0.38, 2025 -0.21, 2026 +0.48 %; the ungated ETH arm's longest drawdown was 586 days (recon_summary.txt:40). 4) Not i.i.d.: 50.5% of entries open with another position (up to 6 same-direction shorts on 2025-11-21), and the half-after-loss rule makes each trade's SIZE depend on the previous closed outcome, so resampling individual values breaks that serial structure; an i.i.d. bootstrap understates the dispersion of live means (10th percentile too high). A block or sequence-preserving resample would be more faithful; the halved values are baked in as observed. 5) Heavy skew: median -1.02%, win rate 38.6%; 15 targets carry the mean. 6) The live halving query has no age limit and no gate-era split (runner.py:80-84): once gated-era closed rows exist it reads them; ETH has had 0 live trades so far, so this does not bite yet. The live query orders by COALESCE(actual_exit_time, exit_time) (fixed 2026-09-13); rows closed before that fix could have halved differently. 7) Exact-6h cooldown ties: 20 taken entries are exactly 6h after the previous taken entry; they pass per code, but if missed live the taken set shrinks (tie-blocked sensitivity: 165 taken) and halving assignments shift. 8) Stops fill at the stop price with no gap slippage; 10 bp measured cost (ETH measured 10.0 bp, CI90 8.0-11.9, calibration log :64). 9) Snapshot bars, not live feed. 10) The calibration log (:61) notes the ETH kill rule (< +0.3R after 15 trades) was set on OKX-gated pools and needs its own decision; this baseline (+0.706% of capital per trade, ungated, with halving) is a different quantity from that R threshold.
bot_chento_v3_eth.notes:
Both counts and totals reproduce the reconciled review exactly: BTC 198 taken (10 tilt skips, 0 cooldown skips, 5 at cap), sum +290.391% vs review +290.391%; ETH 184 taken (106 halved, 0 ambiguous, 1 at cap), sum +129.957% (4-dp list sums to 129.956) vs review +129.957%. Per-exit-year sums also match the review's per-year table (BTC 2026 -6.30, ETH 2025 -8.84). The sequence and sizing came from recon.py's load/select/size, imported unchanged. Nothing was tuned. Every write went to the scratchpad (baseline_chento/). prod.db was opened read-only once, to cross-check.

Live-ledger cross-check (prod.db, read-only): the 3 distinct live BTC trades (each booked twice) were closed at 18 bp before the 2026-09-12 cost change. Re-costed to 10 bp with 100*(pnl_usdt + size_usdt*8/10000)/10000, they reproduce the research values:
- SJ-4244: 2.3458 vs research 2.3450
- SJ-4249: -2.08661 vs -2.08661 (exact)
- SJ-4246: 1.5892 vs 1.5675. Live filled its 72h time stop at 78860.54, which is above the research bar close.
Sizes match notional_x*10k exactly (for example 8611.81 = 0.86118x). So the formula 'pnl_usdt / 10,000 * 100' is the same quantity as these values.

For reference only, not a recommendation: 10th percentile of i.i.d. resampled means (20k draws, seed 0):
- BTC: n=5 -1.17, n=10 -0.42, n=20 +0.15, n=30 +0.37 %
- ETH: n=5 -1.06, n=10 -0.59, n=20 -0.21, n=30 -0.05 %

Points for whoever wires the dashboard warning:
(a) Compare only rows from the gate-off restart on, bar 2026-09-14 08:45 UTC (docs/calibration/chento_triple_v3.md:60). Earlier rows are OKX-gated, and rows closed before 2026-09-12 carry 18 bp (:64).
(b) Exclude or deduplicate the 6 double-booked 2026-08-21/22 BTC rows (3 signals x 2).
(c) The i.i.d. bootstrap understates the dispersion of a live mean, for two reasons. Trades stack in same-direction re-fires about 6h apart (about half of all entries open with another position). ETH position size depends on the previous closed trade's outcome. So the 10th-percentile threshold is too high, and AMBER will fire more often than 10% by chance. The baseline is also mostly in-sample (only 6 BTC / 2 ETH taken trades after the 2026-07-20 P1 cutoff) and non-stationary: BTC's 2026 exit-year mean is -0.18%, against +1.47% over the full period. Early AMBER on BTC is plausible without any defect.
(d) The distributions are strongly right-skewed (medians -0.72% BTC, -1.02% ETH). Means at small n depend on whether a roughly +12% 6R target hits.
